Q120306.t: Canada's highest summit, afloat on a sea of ice
Q120306.s: Nothing about Mount Logan is small. Its summit plateau runs for roughly 20 km, and the massif is thought to have the broadest base of any non-volcanic mountain on Earth. At 5,959 m it is the highest point in Canada, rising out of the glaciers of the St. Elias Mountains and still only about five kilometres short of your cruise height.
Q120306.w: A huge, flat-topped white massif above a maze of glaciers, inland from the Gulf of Alaska near the Yukon–Alaska border.
f: It is named after William Logan, founder of the Geological Survey of Canada.
In North America only Denali, in Alaska, is higher.
Its glaciers lie in Kluane National Park, part of a UNESCO World Heritage site shared with Alaska.

q.q: Which is the only North American peak higher than Mount Logan?

Q870063.t: Where the Himalayas make their last snowy stand
Q870063.s: At the far eastern end of the Himalayas, just before the mountains bend south into the tropics, one pyramid still carries heavy snow. Hkakabo Razi, 5,881 m, is the highest mountain in Myanmar and in all of Southeast Asia. Its slopes fall from glaciers to dense subtropical forest, and the area is so remote that the first confirmed ascent came only in 1996.
Q870063.w: White peaks rising from dark, forested ridges in Myanmar's far north, close to the borders with India and China.
f: It is the highest mountain in Southeast Asia.
The first confirmed ascent, in 1996, was made by Japanese climber Takashi Ozaki and Tibetan climber Nyima Gyaltsen.
Meltwater from its glaciers feeds the headwaters of the Irrawaddy, Myanmar's great river.

q.q: When was Hkakabo Razi first climbed?

ne-pk-1159105475.t: The snowy crown over the Silk Road oases
ne-pk-1159105475.s: Silk Road caravans owed their water to ice like this. Kangze'gyai, 5,808 m, is the highest summit of the Qilian Mountains, the snowy wall on the north-eastern rim of the Tibetan Plateau. Its meltwater runs down to the Hexi Corridor, a chain of oases squeezed between these ridges and the Gobi, which the old trade route followed towards Central Asia.
ne-pk-1159105475.w: Snow-streaked ridges and small glaciers between the brown Tibetan uplands and a flat, desert-edged corridor to the north.
f: The Qilian Mountains run for roughly 800 km along the border of Qinghai and Gansu.
Qilian is thought to come from a Xiongnu word for 'sky'.
Jiayuguan, the western end of the Ming Great Wall, stands in the corridor at the foot of the Qilian range.

q.q: Which ancient trade route ran along the foot of the Qilian Mountains?

Q578862.t: Permanent snow 40 km from Caribbean beaches
Q578862.s: Palm-fringed beaches and permanent snow sit only about 40 km apart here. The Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta climbs straight from the Caribbean to 5,775 m at Pico Cristóbal Colón, which makes it the highest coastal range on Earth. Its twin summit, Pico Simón Bolívar, is practically the same height, and the massif stands alone, cut off from the Andes by lowlands.
Q578862.w: An isolated, often cloud-capped mountain block rising from the Caribbean shore behind the city of Santa Marta, east of Barranquilla.
f: The massif spans almost every climate zone, from tropical coast to glacier.
The Kogi, Arhuaco and Wiwa peoples live on its slopes and call it the heart of the world.
Pico Cristóbal Colón is named after Christopher Columbus.

q.q: What record does the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta hold?

Q238147.t: Mexico's 'star mountain', seen from the Gulf coast
Q238147.s: On a clear day this white cone shows above the coastal haze near Veracruz, more than 100 km away. Pico de Orizaba, 5,636 m, is the highest mountain in Mexico and the third-highest in North America. Its Nahuatl name, Citlaltépetl, means 'star mountain'. The volcano has been quiet since the 19th century, and it carries the largest glaciers left in Mexico.
Q238147.w: A lone, symmetrical white cone east of Puebla, standing well above the volcanic highlands and the green slopes falling towards the Gulf.
f: Only Denali and Mount Logan are higher in North America.
The summit lies on the border of the states of Puebla and Veracruz.
Its Nahuatl name, Citlaltépetl, means 'star mountain'.

q.q: What does Citlaltépetl, the Nahuatl name of Pico de Orizaba, mean?

Q40758.t: Asia's tallest volcano, still breathing sulphur
Q40758.s: A white cone rises above the Alborz ridges, so neat it looks set down by hand. Damavand, 5,610 m, is Iran's highest mountain and the tallest volcano in Asia. Near the top, vents still breathe sulphur and warm gas. In the Persian epic Shahnameh, the tyrant Zahhak is chained inside this mountain, and the Caspian Sea lies just beyond the range.
Q40758.w: A lone snow-capped cone standing above the brown Alborz range, between Tehran and the green Caspian coast.
f: On clear days Damavand can be seen from Tehran, about 65 km away.
Yellow sulphur deposits and gas vents mark the summit area.
In the Shahnameh, the hero Fereydun imprisons the tyrant Zahhak inside Damavand.

q.q: In which mountain range does Damavand stand?

Q1037396.t: Glaciers above one of the lowest basins on Earth
Q1037396.s: The contrast here is extreme. Bogda Peak lifts its glaciers to 5,445 m, while the Turpan Depression, about 130 km to the south, sinks to around 150 m below sea level. Ürümqi spreads along the western foot of this eastern arm of the Tian Shan. Tucked into the northern slopes lies Tianchi, the 'Heavenly Lake', a narrow blue lake framed by spruce forest.
Q1037396.w: A three-headed snowy massif east of Ürümqi, with the pale Turpan basin to the south and the Dzungarian plain to the north.
f: Bogda means 'holy' in Mongolian.
Tianchi, the lake on its northern side, lies at about 1,900 m.
The Turpan Depression south of the range is one of the deepest dry basins on any continent.

q.q: What does the name Bogda mean in Mongolian?

ne-pk-1159106095.t: The smoking mountain beside the sleeping woman
ne-pk-1159106095.s: Look for the plume. Popocatépetl, 'smoking mountain' in Nahuatl, is one of Mexico's most active volcanoes, and a thread of steam or ash often drifts from its crater. Its neat cone, about 5,420 m high, stands beside the long ridge of Iztaccíhuatl, whose outline resembles a woman lying down. Mexico City lies about 70 km to the north-west.
ne-pk-1159106095.w: A symmetrical snowy cone, often trailing a plume, next to a long jagged white ridge south-east of Mexico City.
f: The pass between Popocatépetl and Iztaccíhuatl is named after Hernán Cortés, whose army crossed it in 1519.
Sixteenth-century monasteries on its slopes are a UNESCO World Heritage site.
Its current phase of activity began in 1994, after decades of quiet.

q.q: Which volcano forms a pair with Popocatépetl?

Q2648857.t: Andean glaciers at the edge of the endless plains
Q2648857.s: On the eastern side of Colombia's Andes, a short chain of glaciers hangs above the Llanos, the grassy plains that roll on towards Venezuela. Ritacuba Blanco, 5,410 m, is the highest of these peaks and the top of the whole Cordillera Oriental. Below the ice lie páramos, wet highlands dotted with frailejones, silver-leaved plants that stand in the mist like people.
Q2648857.w: A short line of white peaks on the eastern edge of the Andes, with flat green plains stretching away beyond them.
f: It is the highest point of the Sierra Nevada del Cocuy, in El Cocuy National Park.
The glaciers of El Cocuy have been shrinking fast in recent decades.
Frailejones, the rosette plants of the páramo, grow only about a centimetre a year.

q.q: Ritacuba Blanco is the highest point of which Andean range?

Q233351.t: An ice-capped volcano above Colombia's coffee hills
Q233351.s: Ice and fire share this summit. Nevado del Ruiz, 5,311 m, is an active volcano whose broad top is capped by glaciers, and a column of steam often rises from its crater, Arenas. Around it stretch the páramos of Los Nevados National Park. Lower down begin the steep green hills of the coffee region, a landscape listed by UNESCO.
Q233351.w: A broad, white-capped dome, sometimes steaming, rising above green ridges south-east of the city of Manizales.
f: Its summit crater is called Arenas.
Colombia's Coffee Cultural Landscape, on the hills below the volcano, joined the UNESCO list in 2011.
Its ice cap has shrunk sharply since the middle of the 20th century.

q.q: Which crop shapes the landscape on the hills below Nevado del Ruiz?

Q21519918.t: A white wall above the lake that never freezes
Q21519918.s: Behind the town of Karakol the Terskey Ala-Too rises like a white wall, and Pik Karakol, about 5,200 m, is one of its highest summits. To the north lies Issyk-Kul, a deep blue lake some 180 km long whose name means 'warm lake': even in the harsh Tian Shan winter it does not freeze. Snow and deep blue meet sharply here.
Q21519918.w: Snowy ridges on the south-eastern shore of Issyk-Kul, the long blue lake cradled in the Tian Shan.
f: Issyk-Kul lies at about 1,600 m and is up to roughly 670 m deep.
Its slightly salty water never freezes, even in winter.
The explorer Nikolai Przhevalsky died in Karakol in 1888, and the town long bore his name.

q.q: Which lake lies at the foot of Pik Karakol's range?

Q217457.t: The crown of a twelve-kilometre wall of ice
Q217457.s: Along the main Caucasus ridge runs the Bezengi Wall, some 12 km of ice and rock, and Shkhara, about 5,200 m, is its highest point. It is also the highest summit of Georgia. At its southern foot, the stone-towered villages of Upper Svaneti are among the highest permanently inhabited places in Europe, at around 2,100 m.
Q217457.w: A continuous white wall of summits on the main Caucasus ridge, south-east of Elbrus, with deep green valleys to the south.
f: The Bezengi Wall carries several peaks above 5,000 m.
Upper Svaneti, below Shkhara's southern face, has been a UNESCO World Heritage site since 1996.
The Enguri River rises from Shkhara's glaciers.

q.q: Shkhara is the highest summit of which country?

Q172070.t: Ice and jagged teeth right beside the equator
Q172070.s: The equator crosses its northern slopes, yet there is ice up here. Mount Kenya is the worn-down core of an ancient volcano, and its jagged central peaks, Batian at 5,199 m and Nelion close behind, are second in Africa only to Kilimanjaro. The country took its name from the mountain, which the Kikuyu call Kirinyaga and traditionally see as the seat of God.
Q172070.w: A broad, dark mountain with a rocky, snow-flecked crown, rising from farmland and forest north of Nairobi.
f: The equator runs across the mountain's northern slopes.
Its glaciers have lost most of their ice since the early 20th century.
Mount Kenya's national park and forest are a UNESCO World Heritage site.

q.q: Which is the highest peak of Mount Kenya?

Q72303.t: A lone giant with an ice cap and an ancient legend
Q72303.s: Few mountains stand so alone. Ararat rises more than four kilometres above the surrounding plains to 5,137 m, a dormant volcano capped with ice, with its smaller twin, Lesser Ararat, beside it like an echo. The Book of Genesis says Noah's ark came to rest 'upon the mountains of Ararat', and tradition has attached the story to this peak for centuries.
Q72303.w: A huge white-capped cone with a smaller, sharper cone beside it, standing alone above brown plains near the Aras River.
f: Lesser Ararat, nearly 3,900 m high, is joined to the main peak by a high saddle.
The summit carries a permanent ice cap.
Its Turkish name is Ağrı Dağı.

q.q: What is the Turkish name of Mount Ararat?

Q20191405.t: The high point of the Koh-e Baba, above Bamyan
Q20191405.s: In the heart of Afghanistan the land folds into the Koh-e Baba, a long, bare range often streaked with snow well into summer. Shāh Fōlādī, 5,048 m, is its highest summit. It towers over the Bamyan valley to the north, where green fields follow the river between red and ochre cliffs. Around the peak there are almost no trees: only stone, snow and sky.
Q20191405.w: A snowy, bare ridge running east–west in central Afghanistan, with the green thread of the Bamyan valley along its northern side.
f: The Koh-e Baba is a westward continuation of the Hindu Kush.
The Bamyan valley at its foot lies at about 2,500 m.
Band-e Amir, a chain of vivid blue lakes behind natural travertine dams, lies west of Bamyan.

q.q: Which valley lies at the northern foot of Shāh Fōlādī?

Q213704.s: Mérida fills a long terrace deep in the Venezuelan Andes, and the country's highest peak rises almost straight above it. Pico Bolívar, 4,980 m, is a sharp rock summit named after Simón Bolívar, with a bust of the Liberator on top. From the city, a cable car climbs to neighbouring Pico Espejo, and at over 4,700 m its top station is one of the highest in the world.
Q213704.w: A dark, sharp summit above a deep valley with a city on its terraced floor, in the north-eastern arm of the Andes.
f: It is the highest point of Venezuela.
A bust of Simón Bolívar stands on the summit.
The Mérida cable car, called Mukumbarí, reopened in 2016.

q.q: Which city lies at the foot of Pico Bolívar?

Q221666.t: Equatorial ice on the Mountains of the Moon
Q221666.s: Ice on the equator sounds impossible, yet the Rwenzori range carries glaciers, and Mount Stanley is its highest block. Its top, Margherita Peak, at about 5,000 m, is the third-highest point in Africa after Kilimanjaro and Mount Kenya. Cloud hides the massif on most days, and it has long been linked with Ptolemy's legendary 'Mountains of the Moon', the source of the Nile.
Q221666.w: A cloud-wrapped massif with white patches of ice, rising on the Uganda–Congo border west of Lake George.
f: The mountain is named after the explorer Henry Morton Stanley.
Its main summits were first climbed in 1906 by an expedition led by the Duke of the Abruzzi.
Margherita Peak is named after Queen Margherita of Italy.

q.q: Who is Margherita Peak, Mount Stanley's summit, named after?

Q1045888.t: The highest island summit on Earth, with tropical ice
Q1045888.s: In 1623 the Dutch navigator Jan Carstensz reported snow on a mountain near the equator, and people back home laughed. He was right. Puncak Jaya, 4,884 m, is the highest peak of New Guinea and of any island on Earth. Its grey limestone walls still hold small, fast-shrinking glaciers, surrounded by rainforest that runs down towards the sea.
Q1045888.w: Grey limestone cliffs with small white patches of ice, rising above a sea of green forest in the centre of New Guinea.
f: It was first climbed in 1962 by a team led by Heinrich Harrer.
It is often called the highest point between the Himalayas and the Andes.
It is also known as Carstensz Pyramid, after the navigator who reported its snow.

q.q: Who first reported snow on Puncak Jaya, in 1623?

Q210252.t: Eurasia's tallest active volcano, a near-perfect cone
Q210252.s: Eruptions here are almost routine. Klyuchevskaya Sopka, 4,750 m, is the highest active volcano in Eurasia, a steep, nearly perfect cone that often sends ash plumes drifting over Kamchatka. It rises from a crowded family of about a dozen volcanoes, and its snow is frequently streaked grey with fresh ash. From cruise height its crater is only about six kilometres below.
Q210252.w: A tall, symmetrical snow cone, often with a plume, in a cluster of volcanoes beside the broad Kamchatka River valley.
f: It is named after the village of Klyuchi at its foot.
It belongs to the 'Volcanoes of Kamchatka' UNESCO World Heritage site.
Its height changes by tens of metres as eruptions build up or blast away the summit.

q.q: On which peninsula does Klyuchevskaya Sopka stand?

Q13171265.t: A summit named after the hero of a vast epic
Q13171265.s: The Kyrgyz epic Manas is among the longest poems ever recorded, and this summit carries its hero's name. At 4,482 m, Manas Peak crowns the Talas Ala-Too, a rugged western arm of the Tian Shan with small glaciers and deep gorges. North of the ridge the mountains drop towards the Kazakh plains, where the Aksu-Zhabagly reserve has guarded the slopes since 1926.
Q13171265.w: A snowy knot of summits at the western end of the Tian Shan, where green valleys open north onto the plains of southern Kazakhstan.
f: Some versions of the Manas epic run to hundreds of thousands of lines.
Aksu-Zhabagly, founded in 1926, is the oldest nature reserve in Central Asia.
Near the town of Talas, east of the peak, a 14th-century mausoleum is traditionally called the tomb of Manas.

q.q: Who is Manas in Kyrgyz culture?
q.a: The hero of a national epic
